S34.02.needs: a Free account or a paid account with at least two saved chats that contain a shared word
S34.02.note: Chat search runs on the search route (app/(app)/search.tsx), which renders ChatsListScreen in search-only mode.
steps: Tap the button labelled "Open navigation drawer".
Tap the search icon labelled "Search" at the top of the menu.
Type a word from the title or text of an older chat into the box labelled "Search".
Look for chats whose title or message text contains that word. Tap one and check that it opens that chat. Compare with Expected.
S34.02.where: Open navigation drawer > Search (icon at the top of the menu) > type in the Search box

S34.03.needs: a Cloud account with at least one project that has a description
S34.03.note: The search box is hidden when the Shared filter is chosen; the filter choice appears only in Cloud mode.
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer".
Tap "Projects".
Type part of a project's name into the box labelled "Search projects" and check that the project appears.
Clear the box, type a word from a project's description, and check that the project appears. Tap it to open it and compare with Expected.
S34.03.where: Open navigation drawer > Projects > type in the Search projects box

S34.04.needs: a Library with at least two saved files or images with different names
S34.04.note: The Library search box is the only search control found for these items; the search text is applied after a short debounce.
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer".
Tap "Library".
Type part of a file name or image prompt into the box labelled "Search library".
Check that only matching items stay in the list. Type text that matches nothing and check the empty state. Compare with Expected.
S34.04.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > Search library

S34.05.needs: at least one saved artifact (for example a code file or a chart made in chat)
S34.05.note: The separate Artifacts gallery route (app/(app)/artifacts) has no search box in the code; artifact search is in the Library.
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer", then "Library".
Tap the filter chip "Artifacts".
Type part of an artifact's title or content into the box labelled "Search library".
Check that matching artifacts stay in the list. Tap one to open it and compare with Expected.
S34.05.where: Open navigation drawer > Library > Artifacts (filter chip) > Search library

S34.06.needs: a Cloud account and an outside account for the work source (for example Google)
S34.06.note: The connector names (Drive, Slack, Notion) were not checked against the code; the connector list is in the Connectors screen.
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer", then "Settings", then "Connectors".
Pick a connector, sign in, and wait until it shows "Connected".
Open a chat, tap "Add to chat", then tap "Connectors" and turn on the connected source.
Ask a question whose answer is in that source. Check that the answer uses it and lists it among the sources. Compare with Expected.
S34.06.where: Settings > Connectors (connect a source), then Add to chat > Connectors (turn it on in a chat)

S34.07.needs: a Cloud account whose plan allows web search, on a model that supports it
S34.07.note: The Web search row in the sheet appears only in Cloud mode when the plan and model allow it.
steps: Open a chat and tap "Add to chat".
Turn on the row "Web search".
Ask a question about recent news or a current fact.
Look for "Searching for" under the question, then an answer with citations. Compare with Expected.
S34.07.where: Add to chat > Web search (turn on), then ask a question in the chat; or Settings > Capabilities > AGI Cloud > Web search

labels.text: The files this project’s chats can read.

S34.19.needs: a Cloud account, a project, and one file to upload
S34.19.note: No mobile control was found that limits chats to only one collection; the search over sources runs on the server (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts).
steps: Tap "Open navigation drawer", then "Projects", then open a project.
Tap the button labelled "Open project sources".
Tap "Add sources" and add a file or text.
Open a new chat inside the same project and ask about the added content. Check that the answer uses it. Compare with Expected.
S34.19.where: Open navigation drawer > Projects > open a project > Open project sources (folder icon) > Add sources

S34.23.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on
S34.23.note: Whether a snippet line appears depends on the provider data; the code reads a snippet when one is returned.
steps: Send a question that needs current web information with Web search on.
Watch the line "Searching for" under the question.
Look at each result card: it shows the page title, the site name and, when known, the date.
Compare the card text with what you see when you tap the card (S34.27). Compare with Expected.
S34.23.where: Chat with Web search on (see S34.07), then look under the answer at the "Searching for" line and the result cards

S34.24.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on
steps: Send a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Tap the pill labelled "Sources" under the answer (it can show a count of sources).
Check that each source is a card with the page title, the site name and a link.
Tap a card to see that it opens the page. Compare with Expected.
S34.24.where: Chat with Web search on (see S34.07) > tap the "Sources" pill under the answer

S34.25.needs: a chat answer with citations (Web search on)
S34.25.note: The phone has no hover; the tap is the only preview action. The snippet shows only when the source has one.
steps: Open an answer that shows citation chips (small numbered links) in the text.
Tap one chip.
Check that a box opens with the source title, the site, and a snippet of text, with the buttons "Cancel" and "Open page".
Tap "Cancel" and check that you are still on the same answer. Compare with Expected.
S34.25.where: Chat with an answer that has citations > tap a numbered citation chip in the answer

S34.26.needs: a chat answer with at least four sources (Web search on)
S34.26.note: The code splits sources into cited and other sources; a separate "used" versus "consulted" label was not found.
steps: Tap the "Sources" pill under an answer that has several sources.
Check that the full list opens in a sheet, with the heading "Sources" and, when cited, a section headed "Citations" and one headed "More".
Scroll to the bottom of the list and check that every source is there.
Close the sheet with "Close" and compare with Expected.
S34.26.where: Chat with sources > tap the "Sources" pill under the answer; the full list opens with the heading "Sources" (or "Sources so far" while the answer is still running)

S34.27.needs: a chat answer with sources (Web search on)
S34.27.note: A source with no http link cannot be opened and is shown as plain text.
steps: Open the "Sources" list under an answer.
Tap one source row or card.
Check that the page opens in the in-app browser with the title and address of that source.
Go back to the chat and check that the answer is still there. Compare with Expected.
S34.27.where: Chat with sources > tap a source card in the "Sources" list, or tap a citation chip then "Open page"

S34.31.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on
S34.31.note: Only a publication date is shown (from page_age); a retrieval date was not found in the code.
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and tap the "Sources" pill.
Look under the site name of each source card for a date.
Compare the dates with the page dates you see when you open the source.
Check that a source with no date shows no date line. Compare with Expected.
S34.31.where: Chat with Web search on > tap the "Sources" pill under the answer; the date sits under each card's site name

S34.32.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on; a query with no results (a provider outage is hard to trigger)
S34.32.note: A provider being unavailable is reported through the same notices; a separate unavailable text was not found in the mobile code.
steps: Ask a question that web search cannot answer, such as a made-up name.
Look at the search line: it shows "No results for" followed by your query.
Look under the answer for the notice "Web search didn't return results for this turn" with a "Retry" button.
If the search fails, check for "The search failed. Try sending the message again." Compare with Expected.
S34.32.where: Chat with Web search on > ask a question that finds nothing, or where the search fails; read the line under the search and the notice under the answer
